findings.summary: The table says the user never sees an indirect injection, but indirect payloads can be visible, for example text on a rendered page or in an email body.
findings.evidence: User sees it | Yes | Never; "Indirect vs direct? Hidden in fetched content; the user never sees it"
findings.fix: Change "Never" to "Usually not" or "Often hidden". Say indirect injection is defined by the source (third-party content), not by whether the user can see it.

findings.summary: The pattern bullets tell the learner to run cheap guards first and also to run them in parallel, which reads as contradictory, and the bullet holds two ideas.
findings.evidence: "Cheap guards first, expensive only if needed, in parallel"
findings.fix: Split into two bullets: "Cheap guards first; call the model guard only if needed" and "Independent guards run in parallel".

findings.summary: One bullet packs three separate controls into a single line.
findings.evidence: "Per-agent tool allowlist, read-only creds, narrow scopes"
findings.fix: Put each control on its own bullet, or add a row to the tier table.

findings.summary: The per-span field list is split across two overlapping bullets and mixes several ideas.
findings.evidence: "Per span: redacted input/output, model and version, prompt template version" / "Also: tokens, latency, cost, tool args/results, guardrail verdicts"
findings.fix: Replace both with a two-column table of span field and why it matters.

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "regressions", "production").
findings.evidence: Interview Point: Summarise the full defence-and-measure loop: which controls prevent injection damage, which metrics detect RAG regressions, and which trace fields let you debug production incidents?
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: The lethal trifecta legs are named differently on page 6 than on page 1.
findings.evidence: Page 1: "Private data / Untrusted content / Exfil channel"; page 6: "private data, untrusted input, exfiltration channel"
